title: IELTS Academic 20 - Listening Test 2 - Part 3
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 3

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

13:58ANNOUNCER: Part 3. You will hear two students called Rosie and Colin discussing their human geography assignment.
14:08ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25.
14:38ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
14:47ROSIE: Colin, I'm really struggling to think of a topic for our human geography assignment.
14:51COLIN: Me too, Rosie. I'll tell you what. Let's think about the different aspects of human geography and see if we can narrow the topic down a bit to help us decide.
15:01ROSIE: OK.
15:02COLIN: So one aspect is population. That would be all about population density and migration and so on. Lots of facts and statistics. Maybe a bit boring?
15:11ROSIE: Yeah, but quite straightforward to find on the internet.
15:15COLIN: I suppose so.
15:17ROSIE: How about health? I'd never thought about the links between that and geography until Professor Lee gave us that lecture on cholera. How in the 19th century, a physician used street plans and plans of water supplies to find the source of a cholera epidemic.
15:31COLIN: Yes, fascinating, wasn't it?
15:34ROSIE: Or we could do something more general, like economies.
15:38COLIN: So how financial and commercial factors are linked to the physical environment?
15:42ROSIE: Yeah.
15:43COLIN: I thought that had been taken off the syllabus for this year. ROSIE: Has it? COLIN: I'm not sure. But it might be best to avoid it.
15:49ROSIE: Okay. Maybe we could do something on culture. We had that lecture about culture and geography last week.
15:57COLIN: I didn't get much out of that. It was all so general. And the lecturer didn't give any useful examples.
16:03ROSIE: Yeah, I hardly took any notes. It didn't seem worth it. Me neither.
16:08COLIN: We could focus on poverty. That's something that's a global problem.
16:12ROSIE: The trouble is, Dr. Lee was saying, that you have to be careful with some of the figures relating to poverty. They're sometimes deliberately manipulated.
16:20COLIN: You mean the information gets changed for political reasons?
16:24ROSIE: That sort of thing, yes.
16:28ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30.
17:10ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
17:17COLIN: So what are we going to do our assignment on?
17:20ROSIE: I'll tell you what. One of the possibilities we haven't discussed is urbanisation. And now over half the world's population lives in cities. That's really important.
17:30COLIN: OK, good idea, Rosie. Let's do that. I love living in a big city, but of course there are problems.
17:36ROSIE: Things like theft and robbery? Yes, but where I come from, that's linked to another more serious issue, which is that a lot of people don't have jobs. That's getting worse and worse. And we also still have quite a lot of people who are homeless, though that's not quite so bad as it was.
17:53COLIN: It'd be nice to talk about some positive developments, like some of the new developments on the outskirts of cities.
18:00ROSIE: Yeah, they've opened some massive new shopping centres outside my city.
18:04COLIN: Yeah, the same with mine. But it's meant a lot of the shops in the city centre are closing down. But the outskirts are ideal for buildings that need a lot of space, like for conferences. They've opened a couple of big ones.
18:18ROSIE: Yes, we've got some too. It'd be nicer to have more facilities for things like football too. But that's not happening where I live.
18:26COLIN: Same in my area. We could include something about developing disused industrial sites. It seems like a good idea, because you're not doing any harm to the natural environment.
18:36ROSIE: Yeah, but aren't the buildings architecturally significant?
18:40COLIN: Not really. And what people forget is that they often used quite dangerous materials, chemicals and things, which haven't been properly cleared away, so the whole site has to be made safe.
18:51ROSIE: Hmm, that can't be cheap, and I bet it's often not budgeted for. COLIN: You're right.
18:56ROSIE: Have you read about Masdar City? In Abu Dhabi?
19:00COLIN: Yes. It was designed to be a green city, wasn't it? That might be a good example of a city which set out to depend entirely on renewable energy. ROSIE: Yes, we should say something about that. It was designed to be totally pedestrianised too, wasn't it? With the transport underground.
19:18COLIN: Yes, and they had big plans for recycling to reduce waste to the lowest possible level. But let's stick to talking about power sources. Then there's that ecotown in England, Greenhill Abbotts. It set out to conform to the usual principles, sustainability, and so on. A lot of people were against it at first. They said the plans were unrealistic. I'm not sure how far they've got with it.
19:45ROSIE: I'll check.
19:45COLIN: Right. So it looks as if we have a sort of plan.
19:53ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 3. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 3.

groups.title: Questions 21–25
groups.instructions:
What is Rosie and Colin's opinion about each of the following aspects of human geography?
Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–G, next to Questions 21–25.

options.text: The information given about this was too vague.
This may not be relevant to their course.
This will involve only a small number of statistics.
It will be easy to find facts about this.
The facts about this may not be reliable.
No useful research has been done on this.
The information provided about this was interesting.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: D (It will be easy to find facts about this)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'COLIN: Lots of facts and statistics... ROSIE: Yeah, but quite straightforward to find on the internet.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'straightforward to find' = easy to find facts.
• Đáp án đúng: G (The information provided about this was interesting)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'ROSIE: ...until Professor Lee gave us that lecture on cholera... COLIN: Yes, fascinating, wasn't it?'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'fascinating' = interesting.
• Đáp án đúng: B (This may not be relevant to their course)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'I thought that had been taken off the syllabus for this year... But it might be best to avoid it.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'taken off the syllabus' = may not be relevant to their course.
• Đáp án đúng: A (The information given about this was too vague)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'COLIN: It was all so general. And the lecturer didn't give any useful examples. ROSIE: Yeah, I hardly took any notes.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'all so general / didn't give any useful examples' = too vague.
• Đáp án đúng: E (The facts about this may not be reliable)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'careful with some of the figures relating to poverty. They're sometimes deliberately manipulated... for political reasons.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'figures... deliberately manipulated' = facts may not be reliable.

q26.text: Rosie says that in her own city the main problem is

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (unemployment)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'linked to another more serious issue, which is that a lot of people don't have jobs. That's getting worse and worse.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Tội phạm ('theft and robbery') và người vô gia cư ('homeless') có được nhắc tới nhưng vấn đề nghiêm trọng nhất ('more serious issue') là 'don't have jobs' = unemployment.

q27.text: What recent additions to the outskirts of their cities are both students happy about?

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (conference centres)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'COLIN: the outskirts are ideal for buildings that need a lot of space, like for conferences. They've opened a couple of big ones. ROSIE: Yes, we've got some too.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Retail/shopping centres làm cửa hàng nội đô đóng cửa; cơ sở thể thao/football thì cả hai đều chưa có nơi họ sống ('that's not happening where I live. Same in my area').

q28.text: The students agree that developing disused industrial sites may

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (have unexpected costs)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'ROSIE: Hmm, that can't be cheap, and I bet it's often not budgeted for. COLIN: You're right.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'not budgeted for' = unexpected costs.

q29.text: The students will mention Masdar City as an example of an attempt to achieve
options: A. daily collections for waste recycling.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (sustainable energy use)

• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'COLIN: That might be a good example of a city which set out to depend entirely on renewable energy. ROSIE: Yes, we should say something about that... let's stick to talking about power sources.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'depend entirely on renewable energy / power sources' = sustainable energy use.

q30.text: When discussing the ecotown of Greenhill Abbots, Colin is uncertain about
options: B. why there was opposition to it.
C. how much of it has actually been built.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: C (how much of it has actually been built)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'COLIN: I'm not sure how far they've got with it. ROSIE: I'll check.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'not sure how far they've got with it' = uncertain about how much has actually been built.
